name: Baking soda face scrub

card.summary: A home scrub of baking soda and water used to exfoliate and smooth the skin surface.
card.note: Alkaline and abrasive; can irritate skin and eyes.

quick.overview:
A baking soda face scrub is a do-it-yourself paste of sodium bicarbonate and water rubbed on the face to lift dead surface skin and leave it feeling smooth.

Its appeal is that it is cheap and already in the kitchen. Wikipedia describes a little-water paste of baking soda as a gentle scouring powder in general cleaning, which is the property DIY exfoliation draws on; no clinical trials of facial use were found.
quick.how: People mix it with water into a paste, massage it briefly on the skin, rinse and moisturize.
quick.risks: Baking soda solutions are mildly alkaline and the compound is listed as causing serious eye irritation; skin irritation and dryness are commonly reported by users, so patch-testing and avoiding the eyes are typical precautions.

lead: A baking soda face scrub is a home preparation of sodium bicarbonate and water used as a physical exfoliant. Users aim for smoother-looking, brighter skin.
Wikipedia notes that sodium bicarbonate is mildly alkaline in water, is used as a mild abrasive in cleaning and in some mouthwashes, and carries an eye-irritation hazard listing.[1]

angle.text: Users rub the paste onto the face to exfoliate and leave the skin smoother and less oily-feeling.

paras: The scrub is a paste of baking soda and a little water.[1] The same property that makes a low-water paste a gentle scouring powder is what DIY users rely on for exfoliation.[1]
Sodium bicarbonate is listed as causing serious eye irritation, and its solutions are mildly alkaline.[1]
